items.title: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes Given the Equation of an Ellipse

sections.normalized_html: What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of an ellipse with equation [MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{36} + \dfrac{y^2}{25} = 1?]
sections.readable_text: What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of an ellipse with equation [MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{36} + \dfrac{y^2}{25} = 1?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length [MATH: a] and a vertical radius of length [MATH: b] is given by [MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1.]

In the given equation, we have [MATH: a^2=36] and [MATH: b^2=25.]

  • Since [MATH: a^2=36,] the length of the horizontal radius must be [MATH: a=\sqrt{36} = 6.]

  • Since [MATH: b^2=25,] the length of the vertical radius must be [MATH: b=\sqrt{25} = 5.]

So the semi-major axis has length [MATH: a=6,] and the semi-minor axis has length [MATH: b=5.]

Therefore, the major axis has length [MATH: 2a = 2 \cdot 6 = 12,] and the minor axis has length [MATH: 2b = 2 \cdot 5 =10.]
